summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis and cirrhosis was admitted with fever, nausea, and right upper quadrant abdominal pain, concerning for recurrent cholangitis. She was started on intravenous meropenem, which was later transitioned to ertapenem via a newly placed PICC line for completion of a two-week course at home. Imaging, including ultrasound and MRCP, confirmed findings consistent with her known PSC without new biliary obstruction. An EGD showed stable grade II esophageal varices without bleeding, and no banding was performed. Diuretics were adjusted to manage ascites, with furosemide increased to 40 mg twice daily and spironolactone to 50 mg twice daily. She improved clinically, with resolution of fever and pain, and was discharged home with home health support for IV antibiotics and plans for follow-up with her liver specialist and repeat endoscopy in three months.
problems: Esophageal varices without mention of bleeding
